paths.title: Full Stack Developer
paths.matchReason: Your HTML/CSS basics, Git use and interest in web apps give you a head start, and you already built small apps.
paths.dayInLife: You start the day with a short stand-up, then pick up a ticket such as adding a filter to a dashboard page. You write a React component, connect it to an API route and test it in the browser. After lunch you review a teammate's pull request, fix a bug reported by a user and update the database query that slows a page down. The evening is for learning something new, such as authentication or deployment. The work mixes building screens people see with logic and data behind them, so you switch between design details and problem solving.

paths.title: Data Scientist
paths.matchReason: Your Python and SQL basics plus interest in data analysis fit well, and the maths load is lighter than in AI/ML engineering.
paths.dayInLife: You start by checking a dashboard to see if yesterday's numbers look normal. A manager asks why sign-ups dropped, so you pull data with SQL, clean it in Python and find that one channel changed. You build a chart, write a short summary with a recommendation and share it in a meeting. Later you test a simple model that predicts which users may leave and discuss its limits with the team. Most of the job is asking good questions, checking data quality and explaining results clearly to people who are not technical.

paths.title: AI/ML Engineer
paths.matchReason: Python is your strongest skill and you are interested in AI, but you need maths, ML fundamentals and project proof.
paths.dayInLife: You begin by checking the training run you started last night and comparing its metrics with the previous version. You then clean a new batch of data, tune a model and write a short note on what improved and what did not. In the afternoon you work with a teammate to turn a notebook into an API so the product team can use the model. Part of the day goes to reading a paper or documentation to decide whether a newer approach is worth trying. The role is a mix of experiments, coding and communication, and many experiments fail before one works.

paths.title: Data Engineer
paths.matchReason: Your Python and SQL basics are a solid start, and you like building things that work behind the scenes, but you still need Linux, data modelling and pipeline tools.
paths.dayInLife: You start by checking whether last night's pipelines ran on time. One job failed because a source file changed its format, so you fix the parsing step, rerun the job and add a check so the same problem is caught earlier. Later you meet an analyst who needs a new table, so you design it, write the SQL transformation and test it on a small sample. In the afternoon you review a teammate's pipeline code and speed up a slow query. The evening is quiet unless an alert fires. The work is about reliability, so you spend as much time preventing problems as building new things.

readinessQuestions.question: What does len([1, 2, 3]) return?
readinessQuestions.explanation: len counts items in the list, so the answer is 3.

readinessQuestions.question: Which structure stores unique items?
readinessQuestions.explanation: A set keeps only unique values.

readinessQuestions.question: What is the output of print(type({}))?
readinessQuestions.explanation: Empty curly braces create a dictionary.

readinessQuestions.question: Which tag is best for the main navigation links?
readinessQuestions.explanation: nav is the semantic element for navigation.

readinessQuestions.question: Which CSS property makes a flex container's items sit in a row or column?
readinessQuestions.explanation: flex-direction sets the main axis.

readinessQuestions.question: Which clause filters rows after grouping?
readinessQuestions.explanation: HAVING filters groups, WHERE filters rows before grouping.

readinessQuestions.question: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table even without a match?
readinessQuestions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows.

readinessQuestions.question: Which command saves staged changes to history?
readinessQuestions.explanation: git commit records staged changes locally.

readinessQuestions.question: What does git clone do?
readinessQuestions.explanation: It downloads a copy of the repository.

readinessQuestions.question: Which symbol is used to access the address of a variable?
readinessQuestions.explanation: & returns the address of a variable.

readinessQuestions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the difference between a list and a tuple.
readinessQuestions.explanation: Lists are mutable, tuples are immutable.

readinessQuestions.question: In one or two sentences, explain what a primary key is.
readinessQuestions.explanation: A unique identifier for each row in a table.

readinessQuestions.question: Which command lists the files in the current directory?
readinessQuestions.explanation: ls lists directory contents.

readinessQuestions.question: What does ETL stand for?
readinessQuestions.explanation: ETL moves data from sources, cleans it and loads it into a target.

readinessQuestions.question: In a star schema, what does the central table store?
readinessQuestions.explanation: The fact table holds measurable events, linked to dimension tables.

readinessQuestions.question: What does Apache Airflow mainly do?
options: Schedules and monitors workflows as DAGs
readinessQuestions.explanation: Airflow orchestrates tasks in directed acyclic graphs.

readinessQuestions.question: What does a Docker image contain?
options: The app code and its dependencies, packaged to run the same everywhere
readinessQuestions.explanation: An image is a packaged, repeatable runtime for an app.

readinessQuestions.question: What is PySpark mainly used for?
options: Processing large datasets in parallel across machines
readinessQuestions.explanation: Spark distributes data processing across a cluster.

readinessQuestions.question: Which function numbers rows within a group without collapsing them?
readinessQuestions.explanation: Window functions keep every row, unlike aggregate functions with GROUP BY.

readinessQuestions.question: Which measure is least affected by extreme outliers?
readinessQuestions.explanation: The median depends on the middle value, not on extremes.

readinessQuestions.question: A p-value of 0.01 in a hypothesis test most closely suggests what?
options: The null hypothesis is certainly true
The result would be unlikely if the null hypothesis were true
readinessQuestions.explanation: A low p-value is evidence against the null hypothesis, not proof of anything.

mentorResponses.best_path: Based on your profile, Full Stack Developer is the strongest fit right now, mainly because your web basics are ahead of your maths. Data Scientist is a close second if you enjoy analysing data. AI/ML Engineer is realistic too, but plan for 2 to 3 months of maths and statistics first. Data Engineer suits you if you enjoy building the systems that move and clean data, but it needs strong SQL, Linux and data modelling first. Pick one path to focus on for the next 3 months, and revisit after your first project.
mentorResponses.learn_first: Focus on your first-month plan. Spend the first two weeks strengthening the basics for your top path, and ship one small project by the end of the month. Tick items on your checklist as you finish them so your roadmap stays accurate.
mentorResponses.internship: Build 2 to 3 small projects on GitHub, keep your resume to one page, and apply early on platforms such as LinkedIn, Internshala and your college placement cell. Also contact seniors and alumni for referrals. Showing a live project link matters more than listing skills.
mentorResponses.roadmap_review: Keep the foundation and build stages in the order shown, and postpone advanced topics such as MLOps or system design until year 4. If you are short on time, cut the second project in each stage, not the fundamentals.
mentorResponses.ds_vs_de: A Data Scientist uses data to answer questions and build models, so statistics, dashboards and communication matter most. A Data Engineer builds the pipelines and warehouses that deliver reliable data, so SQL, Linux, Docker, Airflow and Spark matter most. If you like finding insights, choose Data Scientist. If you like building and maintaining systems, choose Data Engineer. The first-year basics (Python and SQL) are the same, so you do not need to decide for a few months.
mentorResponses.default: I can help with your roadmap, skills and projects. Try asking which skill to learn next, how to prepare for internships, or how to balance this with your semester.
